transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-21
Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Elena Torres (Raindrop Head of Partnerships), Derek Wu (Raindrop Cloud Partnerships), Priya Raman (Raindrop Solutions Architect)
---
00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, i'll hand off to Marcus for a little context on the technical side but quick round of intros?
00:12 Elena: Hi all, Elena here, Head of Partnerships at Raindrop Cloud, excited to explore how we might integrate.
00:17 Derek: Derek, I run cloud partnerships, primarily focused on marketplace and network integrations.
00:22 Priya: Priya, solutions architect on infra, i'll be digging into networking and security.
00:26 Marcus: Marcus Lee, SE at Redwood, I focus on runtime and dedicated/private deployments.
00:30 Sofia: Great, goal for today is quick intro, understand Raindrop's partner goals and infra constraints, then map to Redwood integration patterns and potential pilot.
01:05 Elena: High level, we want to offer customers a turnkey inference option on Raindrop, could be a managed Redwood offering in marketplace or a co-managed dedicated option. Main asks are low-latency for enterprise apps, predictable pricing, and an enterprise grade security posture.
01:22 Marcus: Cool, that's inline with our partnerships. We support three modes: hosted API for quick onboarding, Dedicated reserved pools for partners who want committed capacity, and Private/VPC for air-gapped or regulated customers.
01:36 Derek: For marketplace listing we'd ideally start with hosted to get customers using it, but we have some bigger customers that require VPC peering or private deployment.
01:44 Marcus: Totally, and we often recommend a two-path approach: start hosted for GTM, then offer Dedicated or Private for high-compliance or high-throughput customers. We can also do an automated fallback so if Dedicated is saturated requests route to hosted variants.
02:10 Priya: On the private side the big questions are network egress, peering, and KMS integration. We need assurance that keys stay in the customer KMS (HSM) and audit logs meet our standards. Also SOC2 and ISO certifications are checkboxes for some clients.
02:35 Sofia: We have customers doing exactly that. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs can be exported; we also have an enterprise pack for longer retention. We'll share the SOC2 report and security FAQ after this call.
03:02 Elena: Great, can you give a rough latency and cost profile for the different modes? Some of our accounts are extremely latency sensitive (sub-150ms generation for short prompts).
03:18 Marcus: Sure, very rough numbers: hosted API median p95 for short generations on our curated models ~120-250ms depending on load and model size; Dedicated on pinned model and tuned kernel paths can get p95 down by about 20-40% for the same batch sizes; Private depends heavily on networking and hardware but if you run on equivalent GPUs with our runtime you can match Dedicated. Important caveat: sequence length, prompt structure and KV cache usage—if customers use long chat contexts we'll see different tails.
04:05 Derek: When you say KV cache, are you talking about prefix caching across requests? How is that handled across tenants?
04:14 Marcus: Yes, prefix and KV caching—our serving runtime can cache common prefixes and reuse KV cache for sessions. For multi-tenant hosted, caches are logically isolated per tenant; for Dedicated you get a private pool so caching is effectively dedicated to the customer's workload which improves hit rates. There are tradeoffs for memory.
04:55 Priya: For private deployments do you ship a control plane or is it fully customer-managed? Network wise, VPC peering or private link?
05:06 Marcus: We offer an optional private control plane with a customer-managed network boundary. Connectivity can be via VPC peering, PrivateLink, or an on-prem appliance for air-gapped. Control plane still coordinates model versions and rollouts unless you choose the fully air-gapped package.
05:33 Elena: On the go-to-market side, we want a clear partner workflow: listing in marketplace, joint marketing, and an ops-runbook for onboarding customers. Do you have a one-pager?
05:46 Sofia: Yes, we'll send a partner one-pager and a joint-ops deck. That will include onboarding steps, guardrails for pricing, and recommended pilot templates.
06:02 Derek: For pilots, can you provide benchmarking scripts? We like customers to run latency and cost comparisons on sample workloads.
06:10 Marcus: Absolutely, we have a benchmark spreadsheet and a small load harness we can share. It includes tests for throughput, p95 latency across model families, and quantization profiles. We'll pre-fill with typical numbers but recommend running with your real prompts.
06:45 Priya: Security followups: SAML SSO for RBAC, SCIM for provisioning, and logs to our SIEM. Also need to validate data at rest encryption and token handling.
06:58 Sofia: On SSO/SCIM we support SAML and OIDC and can integrate provisioning. We also support bringing-your-own-KMS and full audit logs. We'll attach the security checklist to the follow-up packet.
07:20 Elena: Any concerns about competitor lock-in? Some partners have bedrock or lambda labs integrations already.
07:30 Sofia: We try to be complementary—partners can choose to offer multiple model backends. Our differentiation is operational controls and predictable economics for inference. If Raindrop wants to position this as high-performance/low-cost we can help build that messaging.
08:05 Derek: For billing, are you offering an API metered usage or partner revenue share for marketplace listings?
08:15 Sofia: Both are possible. For marketplace we usually propose an initial revenue share + usage reporting and then can move to a committed Dedicated contract for bigger customers with monthly minimums. We'll include typical commercial templates in the one-pager.
08:40 Marcus: Technical note — quantization matters. We can recommend quantization profile options per model to reduce GPU memory and cost while keeping quality. For some workloads int8 is a good balance.
09:05 Priya: Good, we have customers that require deterministic output and some that care about hallucination rates. Do you provide eval hooks or quality monitoring?
09:14 Marcus: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and eval suites tied to prompt sets. We can set regression alerts and tie them to rollbacks in rollouts.
09:40 Elena: Excellent. On the timeline, we'd like a short pilot in Q2, assuming security checks go smoothly. Is that feasible?
09:50 Sofia: Feasible. Proposed timeline: partner docs and network info in week 1, technical deep dive week 2, pilot kickoff week 3. We can be flexible.
10:10 Derek: Who should we loop in from your side for procurement/legal?
10:16 Sofia: I'll include our commercial lead and the security/compliance contact in the follow-up thread. For procurement templates we have standard MSA and DPA drafts.
10:30 Priya: One specific question: do you support bringing your own model repo or only models managed by Redwood? Some enterprise clients want to bring in their private fine-tuned models.
10:45 Marcus: For Dedicated and Private we support loading customer models; we also support private model repos behind customer auth. Hosted supports curated and vetted open models; for private fine-tuned models we'd recommend Dedicated or Private to meet security controls.
11:10 Elena: Any hard blockers you see on our side to go forward?
11:18 Priya: From my perspective, we'll need network diagrams, KMS detail, and assurance on audit log formats. Also want to validate the control plane access model.
11:30 Sofia: Noted — we'll provide those. We'll also include a small checklist for the pilot: sample prompts, dataset privacy notes, and contact list.
12:00 Marcus: Quick technical point: if you want to include GPU vendor options in marketplace (NVIDIA A100, H100, or AMD variants), we can supply performance profiles per hardware so customers can pick.
12:20 Derek: Customers often ask about H100 performance for LLMs; do you have verified benchmarks?
12:26 Marcus: We have Redwood-verified performance profiles for common models and hardware combos; we'll share the CSV with p50/p95/throughput. It's in the benchmark sheet we mentioned.
13:05 Elena: Great — can you also outline the support SLAs for Dedicated vs Hosted? Some customers need 24x7 support.
13:14 Sofia: Hosted customers get standard business hours support with escalation; Dedicated enterprise contracts can include 24x7 support and accelerated incident SLAs as an add-on. We'll flag the SLA options in the commercial packet.
14:00 Priya: A final infra note: do you run any agents or telemetry inside customer VPCs for metrics, or is telemetry pushed from our side? We need to know what touches our network.
14:12 Marcus: Telemetry is pushed to the control plane; for Private deployments you can keep telemetry internal or export to your SIEM. For VPC peering we negotiate what endpoints are reachable. We'll document the endpoints and ports required.
14:40 Elena: This has been super helpful. Any immediate risks we should raise to internal stakeholders?
14:48 Sofia: Main potential risks: procurement timeline for private deployments, KMS integration complexity for some customers, and initial benchmarking mismatches on latency expectations. We can mitigate with an early technical deep dive and a pre-filled benchmark plan.
15:12 Derek: Ok next steps then — technical deep dive, send partner docs, and schedule procurement/legal intro.
15:22 Sofia: Perfect. I'll send the follow-up email with attachments and calendar invites. Thanks everyone.
15:30 Elena: Thanks all.
